description: A severe storm and tornado warning has been issued for your area. Identify safe shelter quickly and respond correctly as the warning evolves.
objectives: Tell the difference between a watch and a warning
Identify appropriate shelter and move away from windows
Protect yourself correctly during the tornado

steps.title: Tornado Watch
steps.narrative: A tornado watch is issued: conditions are favorable for tornadoes to form, but none has been sighted yet.

options.text: Identify your safe shelter spot now and keep a radio/phone alert on
Ignore it since no tornado has actually been seen
options.mistake: A watch is the time to prepare — waiting until a warning can leave too little time to find shelter.

steps.title: Tornado Warning
steps.narrative: The watch upgrades to a tornado warning: a tornado has been spotted or indicated by radar near your location.

options.text: Move immediately to your safe shelter location
Go outside to look for the tornado first
options.mistake: Trying to see the tornado wastes critical seconds and exposes you to flying debris.

steps.title: Choosing Shelter
steps.narrative: You're indoors. Which location should you shelter in?

options.text: A small interior room or hallway on the lowest floor, away from windows
Near a window so you can watch the storm
options.mistake: Windows can shatter under high winds and flying debris — always move away from them.

options.text: The garage, since it's a separate room
options.mistake: Garages often have weaker structures and large doors that fail easily under tornado winds.

steps.title: Bracing for Impact
steps.narrative: You're in your shelter spot as the tornado approaches. What should you do with your body position?

options.text: Crouch low, cover your head and neck, and use a mattress or heavy furniture for protection if available
Stand upright to see when it passes
options.mistake: Standing exposes your head and body to debris — crouching and covering up reduces injury risk significantly.

steps.title: After the Tornado Passes
steps.narrative: The winds have died down. There's debris everywhere and you smell gas nearby.

options.text: Stay cautious, avoid downed power lines and gas leaks, and wait for official updates before moving around freely
Go outside immediately to inspect the damage
options.mistake: Downed power lines, gas leaks, and unstable structures are common and dangerous immediately after a tornado.

steps.title: Checking In
steps.narrative: You are safe. Communication lines are partially working.

options.text: Send a brief status update to family/authorities and keep phone lines free for emergencies
Make multiple long calls to everyone you know right away
options.mistake: Tying up communication lines with non-urgent calls can prevent emergency communications from getting through.
